status: REGISTERED 2026-10-19 before any perturbation result (no development stage: arms are fixed transformations of existing beliefs)
question: What does a wrong or false maintenance notice cost the anticipatory controller, and does the invariant shield bound the harm? Beliefs from the post-fix 7B extract outputs or the oracle are perturbed (start 1-2 intervals early/late, wrong path, false notice on a world without an event) on the 477 v2 worlds.
primary_metric: obligation satisfaction per episode (as v2), with hard-SLA violation intervals; paired differences against the unperturbed arm of the same belief source and against R0 (R0_phantom for the phantom arms), provider-clustered bootstrap 10,000 resamples seed 0
decision: descriptive: report the cost of each perturbation and whether hard-SLA violations stay at the unperturbed level (shield) or rise; no advance/stop rule

amendments.before: any use of the P_phantom_oracle result (the arm had completed once: its belief was the phantom world's own tuple, whose window is empty, so it behaved as no belief and scored 1.000 = R0_phantom)
amendments.text: Bug fix in scripts/run_maintenance_perturbed.py: for the phantom arms the oracle belief is the original window of the notice, i.e. a false notice with exact timing. The first P_phantom_oracle output is kept under P_phantom_oracle_void_empty_belief and the arm is rerun. Pinned hash updated; no other arm is affected (their beliefs do not depend on the phantom tuple).
